modes.cue_notes: Lie on your back and bring the soles of the feet together, allowing the knees to fall open to the sides. A bolster under the spine supports a gentle chest opening. Blocks or blankets under the outer thighs reduce intensity for tight hips. Allow gravity to do the work: no muscular effort to press knees down.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: The supine version of Butterfly. The bolster under the spine creates a simultaneous chest opener. Kidney and liver meridians course along the inner thigh and groin.

breathing_cues.entering: As you lower onto the bolster, exhale and let the knees drop open. Resist any urge to press them down with muscle effort.
breathing_cues.holding: With each inhale, feel the chest lift and expand over the bolster; with each exhale, the inner groin softens and the knees yield a little further toward the floor by their own weight. The breath oscillates between opening the front body and releasing the inner thighs.
breathing_cues.exiting: On an inhale, use the hands to guide the knees back together, protecting the inner groin before rolling to one side off the bolster.

modifications.name: Blocks under outer thighs
modifications.description: Place blocks under the outer thighs near the knees to reduce the depth of hip external rotation for students with tight groins or hip sensitivity.

modifications.name: Blanket under outer thighs
modifications.description: Use folded blankets instead of blocks under the thighs for a softer, more yielding support that invites the hips to melt progressively over time.

modifications.name: Lower bolster height
modifications.description: Fold a blanket instead of using a full bolster to reduce the thoracic extension component for students with cervical or thoracic issues.

modifications.name: Arms overhead on bolster
modifications.description: Extend arms overhead along the bolster or floor to intensify the anterior shoulder and chest stretch for students ready for more depth.

emotional_release_potential.notes: The simultaneous chest and groin opening invites a quality of receptivity and openness. The lung governs grief and the capacity to receive; this pose can gently encourage emotional availability.
The exposed groin and inner thigh territory is associated with kidney and liver meridians; vulnerability in this exposed supine position may surface primal fear for some students.

The open-hearted shape - chest lifted, arms wide, pelvis open - is anatomically and energetically a posture of trust. Students with difficulty receiving care may find this emotionally challenging or profoundly nourishing.
